approach_A: Take each selected series' reported daily liquid-asset amount divided by its net assets, and blend the three by net assets.
approach_B: Take each selected series' filed daily-liquid percentage column (a share of total assets), and blend the three by net assets.
reason: The vehicle is sized by net assets, so that’s the base for its daily liquidity share.

approach_A: Join the annual filings selected from the financial statements to the submission index on filer and accession, whatever form the index gives them, and count those with a later amendment for the same period end.
approach_B: Restrict the submission index to rows it labels 10-K, join the annual filings to that subset, and count supersession within the index-side set.
reason: A 10-K filter would hide some form mismatches before the two files are joined.

approach_A: Settle every 72-hour window with a start from August 20 to October 27 in date order, and report what the August 25 and October 8 windows recover within that sequence.
approach_B: Settle only the two stipulated windows, starting August 25 and October 8, against the treaty in date order.
reason: The question fixes two start dates, so only those recoveries enter the total.

approach_A: A MIDAS observation has trade and odd-lot volume 'reported' when both fields are non-null; a reported zero qualifies.
approach_B: A MIDAS observation has trade and odd-lot volume 'reported' when both fields are strictly positive.
reason: A reported zero still tells us the field was present.

approach_A: Residual standard deviation is the sample standard deviation of the estimation-period residuals (denominator n-1).
approach_B: Residual standard deviation is the regression standard error of the fitted line (denominator n-2).
reason: The question asks for the spread of the residuals themselves, using the sample standard deviation.

approach_A: Hold the mean coefficients at their preliminary OLS values and estimate the variance parameters by maximum likelihood.
approach_B: Estimate the mean coefficients and the variance parameters together by Gaussian maximum likelihood; the OLS coefficients are the starting values.
reason: OLS supplies the starting coefficients. The likelihood fit can still change the mean.

approach_A: Infer the day-count rule on the bills of at most 182 days, then count 366-day years among all selected bills, including the 52-week bills.
approach_B: Infer the day-count rule on the bills of at most 182 days, and count 366-day years within that same cohort.
reason: “All selected bills” sets the scope for the 366-day count.

approach_A: Total redemptions as the sum of the absolute value of each monthly redemption amount.
approach_B: Total redemptions as the absolute value of the sum of the monthly redemption amounts with the signs as filed.
reason: The monthly redemption figures are already gross amounts, so I’d add them as reported.

approach_A: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals senior plus junior principal divided by 0.90.
approach_B: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals 0.90 times senior plus junior principal.
reason: The loans cover 90% of the collateral, which puts collateral at principal / 0.90.

approach_A: Enter the short rate, long-run level and volatility in the Vasicek bond formula as decimals (4.49% as 0.0449), and convert the fitted level to percent at the end.
approach_B: Enter the short rate, long-run level and volatility in the Vasicek bond formula in percent units (4.49% as 4.49).
reason: The pricing formula expects decimals for both the rate and its volatility.

approach_A: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals 0.90 times senior plus junior principal.
approach_B: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals senior plus junior principal divided by 0.90.
reason: Combined principal represents nine-tenths of collateral value here.

approach_A: 'Its book equity' is the target bank's whole book equity.
approach_B: 'Its book equity' is the book equity of the 20% stake being appraised (20% of the target's book equity).
reason: “Its book equity” refers to the 20% stake being appraised.

approach_A: Days from period end to public acceptance are fractional days measured to the clock time of the acceptance timestamp.
approach_B: Days from period end to public acceptance are whole calendar days between the period-end date and the acceptance date.
reason: Acceptance has a timestamp. Measuring from midnight on the period-end date keeps the fractional day.

approach_A: Count negative net issuance over the quarters that support a quarter-over-quarter change (every quarter after the first observed level).
approach_B: Count negative net issuance over every quarter for which the series has an observation, the first included.
reason: “Those quarters” refers back to the ones supporting a quarterly change.

approach_A: In the Ho-Lee tree, adjacent nodes at one date are 2 x sigma x sqrt(dt) apart (each step moves the rate up or down by sigma x sqrt(dt)).
approach_B: In the Ho-Lee tree, adjacent nodes at one date are sigma x sqrt(dt) apart.
reason: One branch moves up and the other down by σ√Δt, leaving twice that distance between them.

approach_A: Pair a filer's 2021 and 2022 year-end rates by its CIK.
approach_B: Pair a filer's 2021 and 2022 year-end rates by CIK and registrant name together, so a filer renamed between the two filings has no pair.
reason: A renamed filer still has the same CIK.

approach_A: 'Sample denominator' for the covariance is N-1.
approach_B: 'Sample denominator' for the covariance is N.
reason: With N paired observations, sample covariance uses N − 1.

approach_A: The filer universe is the companies in the largest-filer company-facts table.
approach_B: The filer universe is every filer in the annual financial-statement table.
reason: The annual statements define the filing pool. There’s no size cutoff in the question.

approach_A: The normal-equation moment is the design matrix times the OLS residuals, X'(Y - XB).
approach_B: The normal-equation moment is the design cross-product X'X.
reason: At the fitted coefficients, the residuals are orthogonal to X, so X′(Y − XB) vanishes.

approach_A: Compound from one business day to the next, each daily rate applying with simple interest over the calendar days until the next business day.
approach_B: Compound on every calendar day, a weekend or holiday being its own compounding step at the rate in force.
reason: Each business-day rate earns simple interest until the next business day, when compounding resumes.

approach_A: Turn 2 takes every major-disaster designation row in the file as its population.
approach_B: Turn 2 keeps turn 1's population: designations of declarations whose incident began in 2024 with incident type Flood, Hurricane or Tropical Storm.
reason: The county figures still refer to the 2024 flood, hurricane and tropical-storm declarations selected earlier.

approach_A: Gross swap payments are the fixed-leg amounts (hedged quantity times fixed price) summed over all months.
approach_B: Gross swap payments are the sum of the monthly net settlements in the months where the fixed price is above spot.
reason: Months when the hedger receives cash belong in the receipts total. Only paying months contribute here.

approach_A: The share at which the highest fifth begins is the smallest share held by a bank that belongs to that group.
approach_B: The share at which the highest fifth begins is the share interpolated at the 80th-percentile rank cutpoint.
reason: The minimum belongs to an individual bank within the highest group.

approach_A: Estimate the error-correction equation on the whole 2021-2025 weekly panel.
approach_B: Estimate the error-correction equation on the sample through 2023-12-31 used for the long-run relation.
reason: The cutoff applies to the long-run fit. I’d use its coefficients across the full weekly panel for the lagged residual.

approach_A: Store the quarter with a hyphen, as in 2025-Q2.
approach_B: Store the quarter as the source writes it, with a colon, as in 2025:Q2.
reason: The requested YYYY-Qn format includes a hyphen.

approach_A: Report the hedge as face amount held per 100 face of the target.
approach_B: Report the hedge as the multiplier solved from DV01s quoted per 100 face (hedge units per target unit).
reason: The reference position is 100 face of the target. The answer needs the hedge face amount on that basis.

approach_A: 'How many quarters match' counts the quarters where the two series lie within one percentage point of each other.
approach_B: 'How many quarters match' counts the quarters for which a compounded market return can be paired with a revaluation.
reason: A quarter matches when both series have a value. Correlation measures their closeness afterward.

approach_A: Security-level rows are every inflation-protected row with a value in the identifier column, the row labelled 'Total Treasury TIPS' among them.
approach_B: Security-level rows are the rows identified by a CUSIP.
reason: Total Treasury TIPS is a published subtotal, so including it would mix totals with security rows.

approach_A: Distinct causes as distinct stored strings, so '4' and '4.0' are two causes.
approach_B: Distinct causes after reading numeric codes as numbers, so '4' and '4.0' are one cause.
reason: The decimal ending in 4.0 changes the formatting but leaves the cause code unchanged.

approach_A: Lower inverse empirical percentile: the smallest observed value x whose empirical distribution function reaches 0.95 (order statistic ceil(0.95 n)).
approach_B: Lower percentile as in numpy's method='lower': the order statistic at position floor(0.95 (n-1)), counting from zero.
reason: The 95th percentile is the first observed value with at least 95% of observations at or below it.

approach_A: Net issuance transacted is the FA series (seasonally adjusted flow at an annual rate).
approach_B: Net issuance transacted is the FU series (flow for the quarter, not seasonally adjusted).
reason: FU gives the amount transacted each quarter. FA expresses an annual rate.

approach_A: The series name is the first one recorded for that series identifier anywhere in the file.
approach_B: The series name is the one on the filing for the 2025-06-30 yield date.
reason: The June 30 filing identifies the series and supplies its name on that date.

approach_A: Hold the USD 3 million as cash from April 1 and repay no debt.
approach_B: Apply the whole USD 3 million to debt on April 1 and redraw the freed capacity on June 30.
reason: Cash earns nothing here. Paying down the full USD 3 million saves interest until capacity can be redrawn on June 30.

approach_A: Continuing operations is the control number: with a continuing loss, no potential share enters total diluted EPS.
approach_B: Test dilution on total earnings, which are a profit, so the options enter total diluted EPS.
reason: Continuing operations show a loss. On that IAS 33 control measure, the potential shares are antidilutive for every EPS figure.

approach_A: Count settlement days on the depository's calendar, on which Memorial Day (2024-05-27) is not a settlement day.
approach_B: Count settlement days as weekdays.
reason: For the May 24 trade, the holiday pushes the second settlement day to May 29.

approach_A: The modification fees are added to the carrying amount of the continuing liability.
approach_B: The modification fees reduce the carrying amount of the continuing liability.
reason: The liability stays on the books. The fee reduces its carrying amount and is amortized over the remaining term.

approach_A: Draw the repo to its USD 1,000 million limit first, then sell from the securities left unpledged.
approach_B: Choose security sales and repo together, with the sale tranches and the repo both available up to their limits.
reason: Both sales and repo are available at the stated terms, so the withdrawal limit depends on their combined capacity.

approach_A: Store the category in lower case, 'credit'.
approach_B: Store the category as the query writes it, 'Credit'.
reason: The query spells it “Credit” and gives no instruction to change the case.

approach_A: Use the turn-2 distance at full precision as the radius.
approach_B: Use the turn-2 distance as reported to four decimals as the radius.
reason: The radius comes directly from turn 2, before rounding.

approach_A: The severe case replaces the 20% income and collateral reductions with 30% ones, starting from the reported values.
approach_B: The severe case applies 30% reductions to the income and collateral already reduced in the acquisition underwriting case.
reason: The new scenario substitutes 30% for 20% on income and collateral after the same overlay.

approach_A: A filer has 'reported total dividends' only when it tags the total-dividends concept.
approach_B: Where the total-dividends concept is absent, the common-stock dividends concept stands in for it.
reason: “Reported” points to the total-dividends line. A component alone can’t establish that total.

approach_A: After-tax net investment income is the line after income and excise taxes.
approach_B: After-tax net investment income is the net investment income line before the income and excise tax line.
reason: The requested income figure comes after both tax deductions, including excise tax.

approach_A: The common population needs the private non-financial sector debt-service ratio only.
approach_B: The common population needs all three reported debt-service ratios: household, non-financial corporate and private non-financial sector.
reason: An economy qualifies only if it reports the household, non-financial corporate and private non-financial sector ratios.

approach_A: Count filers that tag the broader concept and do not tag the narrow one, whatever the amount.
approach_B: Count filers with a positive dividend under the broader-first rule and nothing under the narrow tag.
reason: Paying a dividend under the second rule means the amount must exceed zero while the first rule reports nothing.

approach_A: Interest accrues on the facility loan left after the sale proceeds repaid debt.
approach_B: Interest accrues on the principal of the investments left in the collateral pool.
reason: The unpaid interest in covenant debt comes from financing the outstanding facility balance.

approach_A: The running peak starts from wealth after the first day's return.
approach_B: The running peak starts from the initial wealth of one, before the first return.
reason: Wealth starts at one, so a decline from that starting point can already be a drawdown.

approach_A: Lower percentile as in numpy's method='lower': the order statistic at position floor(0.95 (n-1)), counting from zero.
approach_B: Lower inverse empirical percentile: the smallest observed value x whose empirical distribution function reaches 0.95 (order statistic ceil(0.95 n)).
reason: At the lower inverse percentile, cumulative frequency first meets or passes 95%.

approach_A: Consolidated gross long-term debt is the face-amount concept, before discount, issuance costs and hedge adjustments.
approach_B: Consolidated gross long-term debt is the long-term debt carrying-amount concept.
reason: The definition starts with face amount and leaves out the three carrying-value adjustments.

approach_A: Turn 4 matches segment goodwill for every annual filer with an entity goodwill figure.
approach_B: Turn 4 matches segment goodwill for the positive-equity filers carried from turns 2 and 3.
reason: Turn 4 compares against the earlier ratio, so I’d keep the positive-equity filers from turns 2 and 3.

approach_A: The numerator is the turn-3 total of holding rows across the issuer's retained filings.
approach_B: The numerator is the largest single holding row reported earlier in turn 4.
reason: The wording asks what percentage the turn-3 row total represents, which puts it on top.

approach_A: Smith-Wilson with one kernel per bond, placed at the bond's maturity.
approach_B: Smith-Wilson in its cash-flow form: a kernel at every coupon date, weighted by each bond's cash flows.
reason: Annual coupons are part of the instruments being fitted, so the curve needs their cash flows.

approach_A: On the ratio scale: the fourteen exact integers.
approach_B: On the ratio scale: the fourteen exact integers and the five named ranges.
reason: The ranges sit outside the integer band but still have a place on the scale. I’d include them.

approach_A: A positive reported DV01 is a gain when yields fall, so the loss is DV01 times the yield rise.
approach_B: A positive reported DV01 is a loss when yields fall, so the loss is DV01 times the yield decline.
reason: A one-basis-point fall gives a gain here. The loss therefore comes from a rise.

approach_A: Financing rate = SOFR + (25 basis points x bid-to-cover).
approach_B: Financing rate = (SOFR + 25 basis points) x bid-to-cover.
reason: Bid-to-cover modifies the spread. Applying it to SOFR as well would inflate the financing rate.

approach_A: The 10% test discounts the new contractual cash flows together with the lender fee paid.
approach_B: The 10% test discounts the new contractual cash flows alone.
reason: The fee passes between borrower and lender, so it belongs in the new cash flows for the 10% test.

approach_A: An issuer is one combination of CIK and issuer name, so a renamed issuer counts twice.
approach_B: An issuer is one CIK.
reason: A name change leaves the issuer’s CIK intact.

approach_A: January's clearing balance starts from the turn-1 opening unrestricted cash.
approach_B: January's clearing balance starts from zero cash; it holds collections, interest and payments only.
reason: I’d start January with opening unrestricted cash, then apply the listed flows. That puts the first breach in February.

approach_A: Sum the schedule rows of the retained filings whose own row date equals the filing's period end.
approach_B: Sum every schedule row of the retained filings that reports a fair value.
reason: The requested cross-section uses marks at the selected period end. Comparative rows describe an earlier date.

approach_A: Sum the schedule rows of that filing dated 2025-09-30.
approach_B: Sum every schedule row under that filing's accession, the 2024-12-31 comparative rows included.
reason: The balance sheet is dated September 30, 2025, so the matching marks come from that date’s schedule.

approach_A: HMDA loan purpose 32 is cash-out refinancing and 31 is other refinancing.
approach_B: HMDA loan purpose 31 is cash-out refinancing and 32 is other refinancing.
reason: HMDA distinguishes cash-out refinancing (32) from refinancing (31).

approach_A: Debt-security rows are the rows whose asset category is DBT.
approach_B: Debt-security rows are every row that carries the C.9 debt-security fields, asset-backed securities and loans included.
reason: Rows with C.9 debt fields qualify even when labeled ABS rather than DBT.

approach_A: Count the information-table rows that hold the CUSIP.
approach_B: Count the distinct filing accessions whose information table holds the CUSIP.
reason: The requested unit is the accession, so repeated information-table rows count only once per accession.

approach_A: Hidden volume divided by total MIDAS trade volume.
approach_B: Hidden volume divided by the MIDAS trade volume against which hidden orders can execute.
reason: The MIDAS denominator covers only volume eligible for hidden execution.

approach_A: Identifiable net assets for goodwill are assets less liabilities less the inherited subsidiary NCI.
approach_B: Identifiable net assets for goodwill are assets less liabilities.
reason: The subsidiary NCI stays separate at fair value because the parent didn’t acquire that interest.

approach_A: Retained payment = the first USD 250,000.
approach_B: Retained payment = the first USD 250,000 plus anything paid above USD 1,000,000.
reason: The layer pays the next 750,000 after the first 250,000. The writer keeps losses on either side.

approach_A: The label is the industry's full name, 'Energy'.
approach_B: The official label is the abbreviation in the Ken French file, 'Enrgy'.
reason: The Ken French file abbreviates this industry as “Enrgy.”

approach_A: A month's index level is the reference CPI dated the first day of the month three months later; reference CPIs on other days are interpolations.
approach_B: A month's index level is the reference CPI dated the last day of the month two months later.
reason: The first day takes the lagged monthly CPI-U directly. Other dates need interpolation between reference values.

approach_A: A January 2024 trade settles one business day later (T+1).
approach_B: A January 2024 trade settles two business days later (T+2).
reason: The move to T+1 came in May 2024, after this January trade, so T+2 applies.

approach_A: Daily NAV return = HiTec return minus the risk-free rate, less the factor-contract payoffs.
approach_B: Daily NAV return = HiTec return less the factor-contract payoffs.
reason: All prior-day NAV is in HiTec. The zero-cost factor positions enter through their payoffs, which are subtracted.

approach_A: A 10-K filed jointly by two registrants counts as one in the cohort.
approach_B: The cohort counts distinct CIKs, so a 10-K filed jointly by two registrants counts as two.
reason: Several parties can share one submission. The submission is the unit being counted.

approach_A: Average balance = total balance divided by the settlement dates on which the security has a record.
approach_B: Average balance = total balance divided by all settlement dates in the window, a date without a record counting as zero.
reason: A missing row gives that date a zero balance. It still counts in the window average.

approach_A: Closing cash is the cash-and-equivalents balance.
approach_B: Closing cash is the balance of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash.
reason: Turn 2 pairs opening and closing cash-equivalent balances, so I’d carry that same closing measure forward.
